a.headline: Adobe's AI text-to-3D world concept is a glimpse of where Firefly could go next
a.summary: Adobe has revealed a concept for text-to-3D world generation that hints at the next evolution of its Firefly AI toolset. For design students, this signals a future where spatial and environmental design workflows could be transformed by generative tools built directly into familiar Adobe software.

a.headline: AI Animation, IP and the Next Phase of Creative Production
a.summary: Generative AI is moving fast from experimentation into professional animation pipelines, raising urgent questions about intellectual property and creative authorship for studios and agencies. If you are studying motion design, this is essential reading on how the industry is restructuring production roles and workflows around AI tools.

a.headline: STUDIO STORIES: Tonic DNA, The Studio That Refused to Be One Thing
a.summary: Montreal studio Tonic DNA has relaunched with a fresh identity and a bet that AI can enhance rather than replace hand-drawn animation, launching a new original holiday special alongside the rebrand. This is a candid case study in how an established creative studio is negotiating the integration of AI into a practice built on craft.

a.headline: Why innovation should be about showing, not telling
a.summary: SpecialGuest creative director Aaron Duffy argues that the most compelling use of technology in creative work is demonstrating ideas through human and playful execution rather than simply describing capability. This is a timely perspective for design students navigating how to work with AI tools in ways that still feel authored and alive.

a.headline: The strongest motion identities encode behaviour, not aesthetics
a.summary: This piece makes the case that motion branding must define systematic behavioural logic rather than relying on surface-level visual style, with AI-assisted tools increasingly deciding default animation behaviour when studios fail to set their own rules. For motion design students, this is a sharp argument for intentional, authored movement systems over aesthetic decoration.

b.headline: Rural Queenslanders have seen gas projects come and go - but a 725-hectare datacentre poses a whole new level of stupidity
b.summary: Residents of Dalby in Queensland are facing the prospect of a 31 billion dollar AI datacentre campus on their doorstep, raising serious questions about land use, energy demand and community consent in the AI infrastructure boom. This is a vivid on-the-ground account of how the appetite for AI compute translates into real environmental and social disruption at a local level.

b.headline: To win over locals, data centers pump $340M into rural Texas projects
b.summary: AI and tech companies are spending hundreds of millions of dollars on community projects in rural Texas to smooth local opposition to massive datacentre developments that bring enormous energy and water demands. This piece reveals the transactional logic behind AI infrastructure expansion and the scale of resource pressure these facilities place on small communities.

b.headline: Rural Data Centers Are in for a Big Federal Tax Break
b.summary: The One Big Beautiful Bill Act could hand major federal tax benefits to hyperscale datacentre projects built in rural US areas, accelerating AI infrastructure buildout with public subsidy. For design students thinking about the systemic costs of generative tools, this is a sharp reminder that AI compute is being actively incentivised to grow at enormous scale.

c.headline: Fjallraven bets on the handmade with giant stitched banners by Miscellaneous Adventures
c.summary: Outdoor brand Fjallraven commissioned Lake District makers Emma and Andrew Groves to hand-sew enormous fabric banners for a major campaign, explicitly choosing slow, human craft over digital production. This is a compelling example of a major brand using analogue handmaking as a direct counterstatement to AI-generated visual content.

c.headline: Busy Bodies brings hand-drawn printmaking to Vimeo
c.summary: Kate Renshaw-Lewis built her animated short Busy Bodies entirely through screen printing and inkjet printing combined with hand-drawn 2D animation, deliberately rooting the work in physical mark-making and independent production. At a moment when AI animation tools are accelerating, this film is a quiet but pointed commitment to labour-intensive, materially grounded practice.

c.headline: Ellie Campbell turns club nights into hand-painted, gloriously wonky animations
c.summary: Ellie Campbell makes painstakingly hand-painted animations documenting underground club culture, embracing imperfection and physical process as central to the work rather than as a limitation. Her practice is an energetic argument for the value of human irregularity and slowness in an animation landscape increasingly shaped by generative smoothness.

c.headline: A new book explores how type became a tool of rebellion
c.summary: Graphic designer and writer Theo Inglis has produced a new book examining the history of protest typography, tracing how letterforms have been weaponised by social and political movements over decades. For design students, this is a timely reminder that visual communication has always carried critical power, and that human-made type carries political history that generated aesthetics cannot replicate.

c.headline: Solo-Made Short Machines Learning Premieres at October Film Festivals
c.summary: Brooklyn filmmaker Anthony Koithra has made a debut animated short called Machines Learning that engages directly with AI as its subject, premiering across multiple independent film festivals this October. Made solo and screened outside commercial distribution, the film positions itself as an independent critical voice on AI at a moment when the industry is racing to absorb generative tools.
